record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
record.context_brief: Perturbing higher-dimensional center dynamics to negative central exponents
record.original_question: Let f be a volume-preserving C^2 partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism whose central bundle E^c has dimension greater than 1 and whose central Lyapunov exponents vanish before perturbation. Is it possible to perturb f slightly to obtain a volume-preserving C^2 diffeomorphism g whose central exponents are negative?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.7. In the above setting, is it possible to perturb f slightly to obtain a volume preserving C2 diffeomorphism g with negative central exponents?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth Riemannian manifold equipped with a smooth volume form. Let $f:M\to M$ be a $C^2$ volume-preserving partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism, so that the tangent bundle admits a $Df$-invariant splitting $TM = E^s \oplus E^c \oplus E^u$ in which vectors in $E^s$ are uniformly contracted, vectors in $E^u$ are uniformly expanded, and the action of $Df$ on $E^c$ is dominated by these two extremal behaviours. Assume that $\dim E^c > 1$ and that all Lyapunov exponents of $f$ along $E^c$ vanish at volume-almost every point.

Question: Does there exist, arbitrarily close to $f$ in the $C^2$ topology, a $C^2$ volume-preserving diffeomorphism $g:M\to M$ that is partially hyperbolic with center bundle of the same dimension and whose Lyapunov exponents along the center bundle are all strictly negative at volume-almost every point?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for the perturbation problem on volume-preserving partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with higher-dimensional center and vanishing central exponents did not surface a resolution. The one-dimensional center case has been addressed (e.g., by Baraviera–Bonatti and subsequent works), while the higher-dimensional center case is repeatedly cited as a remaining problem in surveys and recent works on conservative partially hyperbolic dynamics. No paper announcing a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Conservative partially hyperbolic dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of conservative partially hyperbolic dynamics discussing perturbations of central exponents; the higher-dimensional center case is highlighted as more delicate than the one-dimensional one.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous perturbation result for one-dimensional center is known; the higher-dimensional case is discussed as remaining problematic.

status_evidence.title: A Conservative Partially Hyperbolic Dichotomy: Hyperbolicity versus Nonhyperbolic Measures
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on conservative partially hyperbolic systems still treats the production of negative central exponents via perturbation as an active problem in dimensions of center greater than one.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate perturbations toward negative central exponents in higher-dimensional center settings, indicating the question is not settled.
